When a held piece slips or drops

A slip begins with movement within the grasp. A drop begins when hand support ends.

Grip slip. Small House case and checkpoint. Play this edition’s recording · Exact recording input.

A caught slip has no direct confirmation in the frame review for this take.

Drop a held piece. Small House case and checkpoint. Play this edition’s recording · Exact recording input.

Grip opening, frame 22 (1.83 s) · Fall, frame 23 (1.92 s).

  • Frame 0 The red-and-white rectangular build sits between two resting hands.
  • Frame 8 The camera centers on the approaching right hand and the desk to the right of the base.
  • Frame 14 A long white studded plate protrudes from under the curled right fingers.
  • Frame 18 The right fingers still overlap one edge of the white plate. Its shadow is visible to the left.
  • Frame 20 The white plate and its shadow remain beside the curled right hand, near the edge of the desk.
  • Frame 21 The right fingers remain curled over the plate's far edge. The plate sits visibly apart from its shadow.
  • Frame 22 The right hand abruptly shifts right and spreads its fingers. The white plate is clear of the fingers and visible above the shadow.
  • Frame 23 The white plate appears lower and slightly left of its position in the previous image. The right hand stays open beside it.
  • Frame 24 The white plate rests on the desk, with the tips of the open hand separated from it.
  • Frame 25 The plate remains on the desk in the same place while the right fingers stay spread.
  • Frame 28 The open hand and the white plate remain apart after the fall. There is no visible catch.
  • Frame 33 The right fingers curl back toward the white plate on the desk.
  • Frame 39 The back of the right hand now covers the plate's previous location.
  • Frame 52 The white plate is held horizontally over the red base between the right thumb and fingers.
  • Frame 65 The white plate covers the top of the rectangular build; the right hand has started to pull away.
  • Frame 75 The right hand is clear of the white-topped structure, which remains centered.
  • Frame 87 The finished white-topped rectangle remains on the desk between the separated hands.

Signed November 18 grip-and-fall comparison from v8-2026-11-18.

Attach at a different position or connector. On Halloween Ghost.

An existing connection comes apart · A previously connected piece becomes detached during a scenario that declares the separation unintended. Identify the separated joint and stabilize its host during reconnection.

Distinguish similar pieces · Two available candidates plausibly match the request and the relevant distinguishing feature is unclear. Call out a visible difference in length, colour, holes, or stud pattern.

Miss the initial grasp · The recorded acquisition attempt closes beside the required loose piece and leaves it unowned. Locate two accessible opposing faces and approach again.

Find an available piece · The required loose piece exists in the inventory and the scenario calls for locating it. Describe the design and colour, then indicate a last-seen area or a piece covering it when supported by evidence.

Substitute the wrong design or colour · A distinguishable substitute occupies a required slot while the intended piece remains outstanding. Compare the substitute with the required design and show its distinguishing feature.

Attach at the wrong site · An accepted attachment places the piece at a non-equivalent location relative to the host. Indicate the intended site and the distance or landmark separating it from the current one.

Attach at a different position or connector. On Halloween Ghost.

Repair attempt leaves a problem unresolved · A target already has a recorded problem, an actual repair is attempted, and the original problem persists or the repair creates another. Inspect the residual target or new defect, then propose a different feasible adjustment.

A required part is absent from inventory · A target required by the selected step is explicitly unavailable in the recorded inventory. Check the part ID and other bags, then obtain a replacement or pause.

Request repair guidance · The scenario calls for repair advice, either after a recorded difficulty or as a conditional question. Identify the affected joint, what to release or adjust, and how to check it.

Attach at the wrong site · An accepted attachment places the piece at a non-equivalent location relative to the host. Indicate the intended site and the distance or landmark separating it from the current one.

Attach a non-equivalent module · A distinct connected module is joined where a structurally different instance is required. Show the matching module and a distinguishing feature before changing the join.
